agents.name: Everolimus
agents.explanation: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes.
agents.watch: Report new mouth soreness, cough/breathlessness, fever/infection symptoms, diarrhoea or excessive thirst promptly. A new cough must not simply be labelled drug pneumonitis without checking other causes.
risks: Impaired wound healing and radiation-related toxicity

agents.name: Exemestane
agents.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits aromatase and lowers oestrogen production
agents.explanation: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning can be silent, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

patient.schedule_label: Oral treatment with a planned rest week
patient.schedule_summary: The usual palbociclib starting dose is 125 mg once daily; a lower dose may be prescribed. Palbociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, then paused on Days 22–28 of each 28-day cycle. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily, or fulvestrant follows its injection schedule. Ovarian suppression has its own plan when required.
patient.purpose: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
patient.indication_text: HR-positive/HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an AI, or with fulvestrant after previous endocrine therapy as defined in NCCP. Pre/perimenopausal endocrine treatment requires ovarian suppression; the exact partner and its risks must be confirmed.
patient.administration_text: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2; Day 1 from cycle 3 and extra checks as indicated. Only after at most grade 1–2 neutropenia throughout the first six cycles may FBC monitoring reduce to every three months, before the start of a cycle and as indicated. Renal and liver profile before each cycle; review fever/infection, mouth/bowel symptoms, fatigue, pulmonary symptoms and adherence. No routine palbociclib-specific Day-14 ECG or echo timetable; investigate when clinically indicated.

agents.name: Palbociclib
agents.mechanism: Blocks cell-cycle signals that help cancer cells divide
agents.explanation: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division.
agents.watch: The key early issue is a falling white-cell count, which may cause no symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report infection symptoms or new cough/breathlessness promptly.
risks: Rare but serious interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan

clinical.component_rationale: Palbociclib: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division. Your endocrine partner: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.

evidence.trial: PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3: keep endocrine partner and analysis separate
evidence.population: PALOMA-2: 666 postmenopausal women with ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced disease and no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease. PALOMA-3: 521 women with progression or relapse during prior endocrine therapy.
evidence.comparison: PALOMA-2: palbociclib plus letrozole versus placebo plus letrozole. PALOMA-3: palbociclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant.
evidence.applicability: PALOMA-2 supports the first-line AI context; PALOMA-3 supports the prior-endocrine/fulvestrant context. Neither is an adjuvant regimen.
evidence.qualitative_result: Palbociclib delayed progression. Final protocol-specified OS was not significantly improved in the overall population of either trial; later PALOMA-3 exploratory follow-up must retain its exploratory label.

questions.q: How long does treatment last?
questions.a: The usual metastatic starting dose is ribociclib 600 mg once daily on Days 1–21 followed by Days 22–28 off. Continue the prescribed AI daily or fulvestrant on its own injection schedule; add ovarian suppression when indicated. Continue while beneficial and tolerated. questions.q: Which checks happen before and during treatment?
questions.a: FBC, renal and liver profile, potassium, calcium, magnesium and phosphorus. ECG before initiation; QTcF must be below 450 ms. Correct electrolyte abnormalities and review QT/CYP3A interactions. Confirm endocrine partner, menopause/ovarian suppression, prior treatment and the NCCP indication/eligibility discrepancy. FBC, renal and liver profile every two weeks for cycles 1–2, then before cycles 3–6, then as clinically indicated. questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Take ribociclib once daily with or without food; swallow whole. Avoid grapefruit. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Confirm any clinical hold and restart with the team. The endocrine partner follows a separate prescription. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: How long does treatment last?
questions.a: The usual abemaciclib starting dose is 150 mg twice daily; a lower dose or altered schedule may be prescribed. Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously for up to two years with endocrine therapy, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires an earlier change. A four-week dispensing block is not a rest cycle. Endocrine treatment normally continues beyond abemaciclib. At completion of the planned two-year abemaciclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

questions.q: Which checks happen before and during treatment?
questions.a: FBC, renal, liver and bone profile; ECG as clinically indicated. Confirm node-positive high-risk eligibility, definitive surgery and timing: within 16 months of resection and up to 12 weeks of endocrine treatment after the last non-endocrine treatment before starting. Assess VTE history, bowel function, all medicines, endocrine partner, ovarian suppression if using an AI before menopause, and bone/reproductive health. FBC, renal, liver and bone profile every two weeks for the first two months, monthly for the next two months, then as clinically indicated. More frequent liver monitoring for grade 2 or worse liver abnormalities. ECG is driven by clinical need; no routine ribociclib Day-14 ECG schedule. Early and ongoing diarrhoea review, hydration/intake, infection, clots, breathlessness and adherence; prompt action between appointments. Creatinine can rise through inhibited tubular secretion without a true fall in filtration; assess the clinical context and alternative renal measures if needed.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Take abemaciclib twice daily at regular times with or without food. Swallow whole; do not split, chew or crush. Avoid grapefruit. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose. A clinical hold and restart require the treating team’s instructions. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: What happens after treatment changes or ends?

evidence.trial: NATALEE: primary trial and prespecified six-year descriptive follow-up
evidence.population: 5,101 adults with HR-positive/HER2-negative stage II–III early breast cancer, including selected high-risk node-negative disease.
evidence.comparison: Ribociclib 400 mg on Days 1–21 every 28 days for three years plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor versus the aromatase inhibitor alone; endocrine therapy for at least five years, with goserelin in men and premenopausal women.
evidence.applicability: Adjuvant population; not MONALEESA metastatic evidence. NCCP00892v2 includes selected node-negative eligibility but also a conflicting node-negative exclusion, which still requires clinical reconciliation.
evidence.qualitative_result: The primary trial established an iDFS benefit. The six-year descriptive analysis continued to favor ribociclib for recurrence outcomes and reported a favorable OS estimate with a nominal P value.

endpoints.metric: Estimated invasive disease-free survival at six years
endpoints.result_text: 83.23% versus 77.92%; difference 5.3 percentage points. HR 0.741 (95% CI 0.646–0.849); nominal one-sided P<.0001.
endpoints.interpretation: The previously established recurrence benefit persisted in longer follow-up.
endpoints.analysis_status: Prespecified descriptive six-year analysis; cutoff 15 May 2026; journal pre-proof online 23 October 2026
